method: All 18 source/baseline/after PNG triptychs were opened with view_image at front, three-quarter and side, rest and action. Pixel inspection is a manual comparison, not a numerical fidelity percentage.

observed: Red armor and gold-rimmed shoulder pauldrons, swept helmet horns and brown bovine muzzle replace the generic sword-and-shield warrior.
Both gripping arms, fists, handle and silver double-swept axe remain coherent during the shared weapon pose.
Front/three-quarter/side views show the blade thickness and sculpted body; all extremities fit the final gallery frame.
limits: The reference is a cropped bust; legs, hooves, belt and greaves are declared inferred continuations.
Facial relief, rivets and axe bevel highlights remain simplified procedural facets.

observed: Asymmetric white/teal face, yellow eye star, round red nose, white grin, red collar and purple open hands replace a staff-carrying mage.
Bare swept left brim and curled bell-tipped right crown preserve the asymmetry seen in the JPEG.
A continuous inferred lower tunic replaces an earlier visible torso/skirt gap; hands and forearms share the casting joint.
limits: The lower tunic, shoes and legs continue a cropped bust and are not documented original full-body costume.
The mask and hat use extruded source contours, with adapted depths and simplified facial relief.

The final narrower snout is tapered in real geometry and all wing tips fit the gallery frame at radius 7.0.

scope: Actual source-module comparison under matching scene conditions; no compiled app, native battle outcome or TCG rule completeness is certified here.
